sections.title: Personal Potential in the Past
sections.content: To express what someone *could have done* in the past, attach the potential suffix -hat/-het to the verb stem, conjugate it in the past tense (-ott/-ett/-t), and follow it with 'volna': 'megelőzhettük volna' (we could have prevented it), 'szólhattál volna' (you could have said something).

sections.title: Impersonal 'lehetett volna + infinitive'
sections.content: When focusing on the action itself rather than a specific agent, use 'lehetett volna' + infinitive: 'Meg lehetett volna menteni a beteget' (The patient could have been saved / It would have been possible to save the patient). Note how the preverb 'meg' sits before 'lehetett'.

sections.title: Past Potential Constructions
rows: el lehetett volna kerülni a bajt
the trouble could have been avoided

items.spanish: Időben megelőzhettük volna a súlyosbodást, ha a beteg szót fogad.
items.english: We could have prevented the worsening in time if the patient had obeyed.

items.spanish: Ennél többet a legodaadóbb ápolónő sem tehetett volna.
items.english: Even the most devoted nurse could not have done more than this.

items.spanish: A fertőzést könnyen el lehetett volna kerülni alapos kézmosással.
items.english: The infection could easily have been avoided with thorough handwashing.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: When a preverb verb is used with 'lehetett volna', the preverb climbs in front of 'lehetett': 'Meg lehetett volna előzni' (not 'Lehetett volna megelőzni').
